hunks.baseline: Namho grabbed a rock and charged at Taishan like a mad bison, but his run was quickly cut short.
hunks.sol: Namho snatched up a rock and charged at Taishan like a mad bison, but he didn’t get far.

hunks.sol: At a glance from Jeok Cheongang, Sama Pyo and Song Ilseom appeared like streaks of light and seized his arms from either side.

hunks.baseline: What on earth did this guy think he was?

hunks.baseline: Flustered by Jeok Cheongang’s burning gaze, Hyuk Mujin started rambling.
hunks.sol: Flustered by Jeok Cheongang’s blazing stare, Hyuk Mujin began to ramble.

hunks.baseline: “I mean, a few days ago, you cut down every last one of those bandits. All those men…”
hunks.sol: “I mean, a few days ago, you cut down all those bandits. Every last one of them.”

hunks.baseline: “What am I, a butcher? ‘Cut them down’? And it wasn’t just bandits. River pirates were mixed in, too.”
hunks.sol: “What am I, a butcher? ‘Cut them down’? And they weren’t all bandits. There were river pirates, too.”

hunks.baseline: “Isn’t that basically the same thing?”
hunks.sol: “Isn’t that the same thing?”

hunks.baseline: “They’re distinctly different. Though it doesn’t change the fact that every last one of them deserved to die.”
hunks.sol: “They’re entirely different. Though that doesn’t change the fact that every one of them deserved to die.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang hurriedly changed his answer, but watching him only confirmed Hyuk Mujin’s suspicion.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang hurriedly corrected himself, but that only confirmed Hyuk Mujin’s suspicion.

hunks.baseline: Strangely enough, of all the countless sins in the world, Jeok Cheongang considered arson the worst.
hunks.sol: Strangely, of all the sins in the world, Jeok Cheongang considered arson the worst.

hunks.sol: They relied on their natural talent instead of working hard, then strutted around trading on their sects’ prestige.
